jurisdictions.name: West Hartford (Hartford County)
notes: The town requires all permit applications, including building permits, to go through its CityView online portal; paper applications are no longer accepted.
The town's Building FAQ says it follows the State Building Code, which includes the 2021 International Swimming Pool and Spa Code.
Depending on the project, approval may also be needed from Planning/Zoning, Engineering, Health or the Fire Marshal.

jurisdictions.name: Norwalk (Fairfield County)
notes: Swimming pools are treated as accessory structures that need a Zoning Permit first, then a Building Permit after zoning approval.
The application needs a site plan showing the pool's location relative to property lines at a legible scale, plus dimensionally accurate plans of current and proposed conditions.
Pools in a flood zone need extra documentation, and a flood-zone application may apply.
The page asks for three paper copies of plans, delivered in person or by mail; no online portal is named.

sources.title: Apply for a Zoning Permit - Norwalk

jurisdictions.name: Darien (Fairfield County)
notes: The town says all permit applications are submitted electronically through its ViewPoint online permitting system.
Its Work Requiring a Permit page says a permit is needed to install a pool or spa, in-ground or above ground.
Its online-permitting document list includes a Pool Water Alarm Affidavit and a Swimming Pool Fence Agreement.

sources.title: Frequently Used Documents for Online Permitting - Darien

jurisdictions.name: Shelton (Fairfield County)
notes: The city's building permit procedure covers all construction and lists swimming pools among the permits the Building Official issues.

Listed steps include site plan approval through Planning and Zoning and Inland Wetlands where applicable, a zoning compliance application, and a copy of the contractor's license and insurance certificate.

jurisdictions.name: Greenwich (Fairfield County)
jurisdictions.office: Greenwich Department of Public Works, Building Inspection Division
notes: The town says a new in-ground, above-ground or on-ground swimming pool, spa, hot tub or plunge pool on a 1-2 family home or townhouse needs a Building Permit for Swimming Pool, Spa, or Hot Tub before work begins, and the required safety barrier is included in that permit.
The town's submittal list asks for two sets of construction plans; for in-ground swimming pools or spas, these include structural plans certified by a CT P.E. and a pool piping diagram.

The town's pool permit application cites the 2021 ISPSC and the 2022 CT State Building Code, and asks whether the pool barrier will be a fence or an automatic pool safety cover meeting ASTM F1346 (cover specs go with the application). In its affidavit, the permit holder and owner accept responsibility for a temporary safety barrier under Section 305.1.1 of the 2021 ISPSC before excavation.

The town says the pool permit process starts at the Building Inspection Division counter at Town Hall, where applicants get a Permit Application Sign-off Sheet and Group Number. Depending on the work, sign-offs may be needed from the Health Department, Zoning Enforcement, Wetlands Agency, Sewer Division and Tax Collector's Office.
The town's permit process page says only re-roofing, re-siding and replacement windows for 1-2 family dwellings can be filed by email; all other building permits must be filed in person.

sources.title: Building Permit Application: Swimming Pool, Spa or Hot Tub and Required Safety Barrier (Town of Greenwich)
